meta.name: FocusRecall theme system 2026 (proposal)
meta.note: Proposal only. Resolved values; component tokens alias semantic tokens (see component-map.json).

themes.name: Ivory & Ink
themes.tagline: Brand ivory paper, ink-blue actions, a single amber bookmark.
themes.story: The brand board translated literally: ivory #FFFDF7 is the card stock, Ink #183D56 is the only filled colour, Amber #CC8C30 is reserved for small marks (bookmark, today, streak) so it never competes with content. Text is a deep ink rather than black, which keeps the page warm without looking sepia.

themes.name: Library
themes.tagline: Oatmeal paper, walnut type, oxblood leather and brass.
themes.story: Built from a reading room: bookcloth oxblood for actions, brass for the bookmark, walnut instead of grey for text. Every neutral carries the same brown undertone, so nothing reads as a stray grey. The recall indigo is the colour of an old bookbinding, which keeps it serious next to oxblood.

themes.name: Terracotta
themes.tagline: Sun-baked plaster, terracotta tile, a deep teal shutter.
themes.story: The one deliberately expressive warm theme. Terracotta and deep teal are near complements, so a single teal mark carries a lot of energy without a second bright colour. The plaster background is pink-beige, not yellow, which keeps terracotta from turning orange-on-orange.

themes.name: Saffron
themes.tagline: Cream and saffron with espresso type and a slate bookmark.
themes.story: Takes the brand amber and lets it lead: buttons are saffron with dark type (the inverse of most apps), which feels sunny but not loud. Because a yellow fill is never legible as text, links and labels use a separate deep-ochre "accent text" token — the system makes this distinction explicit for every theme.

themes.name: Matcha
themes.tagline: Parchment with a green cast, matcha olive and a clay-pot accent.
themes.story: An olive, not a "success green": the accent sits at a yellow-green hue that never reads as a status colour. Umeboshi plum for recall and stream blue for rest are both muted to the same depth as the olive so the stage colours read as one family.

themes.name: Celadon
themes.tagline: Celadon glaze, jade actions and a soft clay-coral mark.
themes.story: The lowest-energy light theme. Backgrounds are grey-green porcelain with very low chroma, so long sessions feel shaded rather than bright. Jade is the only saturated colour; the clay-coral mark is its complement, used sparingly. Rest is a sky blue — literally "looking up".

themes.name: Lagoon
themes.tagline: Sea mist, harbour blue and a sand-coloured marker.
themes.story: Cooler and crisper than Celadon: the accent is a harbour blue between teal and navy, surfaces are almost white with a blue-grey canvas, and text is a deep petrol instead of black. A sand-orange mark gives the warm counterweight cool themes usually lack.

themes.name: Cobalt
themes.tagline: White paper, cobalt ink and a sunflower highlight.
themes.story: For people who want maximum clarity: true white cards on a cool grey canvas, a confident cobalt and berry recall. It is the most saturated accent in the library, balanced by completely neutral surfaces. Best on well-lit screens.

themes.name: Wisteria
themes.tagline: Lilac-grey paper, deep violet and antique gold.
themes.story: Violet and antique gold is a classic book-jacket pairing; here violet is darkened until it behaves like an ink, and the lilac tint in the neutrals is kept just below where it would look pink. Recall moves to rose so the two stage colours never blur.

themes.name: Rosewater
themes.tagline: Blush paper, raspberry ink and a sage counterpoint.
themes.story: Soft without being sugary: the blush lives only in the neutrals (chroma under 0.02), the raspberry is deep enough to carry white text, and a muted sage mark keeps it from becoming monochrome pink. Indigo recall gives the cool note.

themes.name: Graphite
themes.tagline: Grey paper, black buttons, a single vermilion signal.
themes.story: Swiss-style minimal: every surface is achromatic, actions are near-black, and colour appears only where it means something — stage colours, charts, and one vermilion mark. Ideal for people who find tinted themes distracting, and the cleanest canvas for subject colours.

themes.name: Ink Night
themes.tagline: Round 2: deep ink, ivory type, a softened amber.
themes.story: The original idea with the volume turned down. The canvas is lifted from 0.21 to 0.25 lightness and the blue undertone halved, so it reads as ink-grey rather than navy. Amber drops from chroma 0.125 to 0.085, so the Start button is still the brightest object but no longer glows. Ivory text sits at about 11:1 instead of 13:1.

themes.name: Ink Dim
themes.tagline: Pewter Dim's lightness with an ink undertone and muted amber.
themes.story: Closest to the theme you liked best. It uses Pewter Dim's surface lightness, so it sits at a dim grey rather than a dark room, and keeps a gentle ink-blue undertone so it still belongs to FocusRecall. Amber is the only warm note, softened to a honey tone.

themes.name: Ink Rail
themes.tagline: Neutral pewter workspace, a deep-ink sidebar, amber actions.
themes.story: Puts the brand in one place only: the sidebar is solid brand ink, as on the logo board, and the workspace is a neutral pewter like Pewter Dim. Content areas carry no tint at all, so subject colours and charts read exactly, while the app still looks unmistakably FocusRecall.

themes.name: Ink Slate
themes.tagline: Slate-blue dim with steel-ink actions; amber only as a mark.
themes.story: Mirrors the light theme's logic: in Ivory & Ink the action colour is ink and amber is only a mark, and here it is the same, with ink lifted to a steel blue that stays legible on slate. It is the calmest candidate, with no warm fill anywhere except the bookmark.

themes.name: Ink & Brass
themes.tagline: Warm graphite, brass actions, an ink-blue Focus stage.
themes.story: A warm-neutral dark, like a lamp-lit desk, with brass (amber taken down to a metal tone) for actions and the brand ink lifted to sky for the Focus stage, so the brand is still present in pressing and doing. The least "blue" of the candidates.

themes.name: Pewter Dim
themes.tagline: A dim (not black) mode: pewter grey with a citrine accent.
themes.story: The reference for every dark theme in round 2. Surfaces sit around 25–30% lightness and text contrast is held near 10:1 instead of 15:1, which avoids halation. Citrine on pewter is a modern, gentle pairing, and the only yellow action colour in the dark set.

themes.name: Graphite Night
themes.tagline: Neutral graphite, a quiet azure, one muted vermilion signal.
themes.story: Kept from round 1 but lifted to dim, and the azure taken from chroma 0.11 to 0.07 so it reads as a calm blue rather than a highlight. Still zero tint in the surfaces, so subject colours and charts read exactly as chosen.

themes.name: Indigo Hour
themes.tagline: Dusk indigo, periwinkle and pale starlight.
themes.story: Round 1 was the most chromatic dark; now the indigo lives only as a faint undertone (0.02), the periwinkle is a soft lavender-blue and the starlight mark is pale. It keeps the twilight mood without glowing.

themes.name: Chalkboard
themes.tagline: Matte slate board, chalk text, pink and blue chalk.
themes.story: Kept and made more matte: chalk colours are now real pastels (chroma ≤ 0.065), the slate is a little lighter, and the Focus stage is a dusty blue chalk rather than ice blue. Pink chalk for actions, yellow chalk for marks.

themes.name: Espresso
themes.tagline: Dim mocha grey, an enamel-blue action, crema mark.
themes.story: Round 1 was a deep brown room. Now the brown is only an undertone on a dim grey, the kind of warmth you notice rather than see, and the enamel blue is very muted. It is the warm counterpart to Pewter Dim.

themes.name: Evergreen
themes.tagline: Moss-grey dim, sage actions, lantern mark.
themes.story: The green is now an undertone in grey stone rather than a forest-black, and the mint accent became a sage (chroma 0.096 → 0.055). It reads as quiet and natural, not "green theme".

themes.name: Aubergine
themes.tagline: Plum-grey dim, dusty mauve, rose-gold mark.
themes.story: Orchid on velvet became dusty mauve on a plum-grey: the elegance stays, the saturation goes. Rose-gold marks give a little warmth.

themes.name: Deep Sea
themes.tagline: Blue-grey dim, a soft coral action, sea-glass focus.
themes.story: Keeps the coral/aqua idea but both are now muted: coral is a dusty shell pink-orange and aqua a sea-glass. The canvas is a dim harbour grey with a light blue undertone.

themes.name: Lichen
themes.tagline: Olive-grey stone, a soft lichen accent, persimmon mark.
themes.story: Chartreuse dropped to a soft lichen (chroma 0.117 → 0.07) on an olive-grey dim stone. Still the one non-blue, non-grey dark, now gentle enough for long sessions.

themes.name: Darkroom
themes.tagline: Low-blue late-night mode: warm umber dim, muted terracotta.
themes.story: Still the purpose-built after-midnight theme with almost no blue emission, but no longer a red safelight: an umber dim with parchment text and a muted terracotta. Charts lean on lightness steps and labels (documented trade-off).
